content_units: Intergenerational Game Night Picks

A good mix for   18 people ages 14 to 72   is a rotation of light, social, easy-to-explain activities with low rules overhead and positive themes. The options below are all learnable in   under 10 minutes  , require   no hobby-gaming background  , and avoid war themes or deception-centered play.
10 Easy-to-Learn Activities and Games
Activity/Game   Ideal Group Size   Noise Level   Why it works for mixed ages
Just One   4–7 per table   Low–Medium   Cooperative word-guessing keeps everyone involved; older and younger players can both contribute through vocabulary and shared knowledge.
Dixit   4–8 per table   Low   Beautiful image cards invite creativity without requiring speed, trivia, or strategy experience; good for different personalities and ages.
Telestrations   6–8 per table   Medium–High   Drawing plus guessing creates lots of laughter; artistic skill is not required, which helps level the field across generations.
Hues and Cues   3–10 per table   Low–Medium   Players describe colors with simple words, so it is accessible, quick, and great for conversation without complex rules.
Ticket to Ride   2–5 per table   Low   Route-building is intuitive and calm; turns are simple, and the theme is travel rather than conflict, which suits broad age appeal.
Qwirkle   2–4 per table   Low   Pattern matching by color and shape is easy to teach and language-light, making it friendly for mixed ages and different experience levels.
Sushi Go Party!   4–8 per table   Medium   Cute art and short rounds make it approachable; choices are simple enough for beginners while still fun for adults.
Blank Slate   3–8 per table   Low–Medium   Matching words encourages gentle humor and shared cultural references without putting pressure on quick reflexes or bluffing.
Bingo with themed prompts or prizes   10–30   Medium   Familiar format, inclusive pacing, and easy hosting make it ideal for a larger community event with varied ages and comfort levels.
Team Charades or Picture Charades   8–20   Medium–High   No materials-heavy setup, easy to adapt for mobility or comfort, and naturally creates cross-age teamwork and laughter.
Best Setup for 18 Guests
Option 1:   Three-table rotation     Split into 3 groups of 6 and rotate every 25–35 minutes   Best for variety
Plan Rotation
Option 2:   One all-group opener + table games     Start with Bingo or Charades, then break into smaller groups   Best for warm-up and mingling
Event Tips
Option 3:   Quiet room + lively room     Put Qwirkle, Dixit, Just One in a calmer space; Charades/Telestrations in a louder one   Best for accessibility and comfort
Group Games
Option 4:   Most balanced shortlist     Just One, Dixit, Bingo, Telestrations, Qwirkle   Best overall mix of calm, laughter, and easy learning
Compare Games
Event Fit Notes
-   Best overall for mixed ages:   Just One, Dixit, Bingo
-   Best if you want laughter:   Telestrations, Charades
-   Best for quieter tables:   Qwirkle, Ticket to Ride, Dixit
-   Best for very quick teaching:   Bingo, Charades, Blank Slate
-   Best if guests may not know each other well:   Just One, Hues and Cues, Bingo
